name: Alberta-Pacific (Al-Pac) Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~650 kt/yr NBSK kraft pulp; largest single-line kraft pulp producer in North America
operator: Alberta-Pacific Forest Industries Inc. (majority owned by Marubeni Corp.)
source: Al-Pac website (alpac.ca); GEM Wiki AlPac Boyle power station; calc: ~0.92 t CO2/adt × 650 kt/yr
notes: Located ~50 km northeast of Athabasca, Alberta (Athabasca County). Section 29, Township 68, Range 19, W4M. Operational since 1993. Co-located biomass power station (AlPac Boyle). Alberta offers deep saline aquifer storage (Wabamun, Cooking Lake formations). One of the flagged missing facilities — priority BECCS candidate. Coordinates estimated from township-range legal description.

name: Mercer Pulp (formerly Domtar) Kamloops Mill
capacity_note: ~350 kt/yr NBSK kraft pulp; two-line mill (A+B lines; B-line restarted 2025)
operator: Kruger Specialty Papers Holding (acquired from Paper Excellence/Domtar 2024)
source: Tissue World Magazine: Kruger acquires Domtar Kamloops mill; Paper Excellence sale announcement 2024; Domtar Kamloops fact sheet 2016
notes: Kamloops, BC on the Thompson River. B-line had been idled; Kruger acquiring to boost NBSK capacity. No CCS plans. BC lacks CO2 storage infrastructure vs. Alberta.

name: Domtar Windsor Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: 645,000 short tons/yr uncoated fine paper; integrated pulp+paper mill (Eastern Townships, Quebec)
source: Domtar Windsor Mill fact sheet 2025; Pulp and Paper Canada Windsor modernization 2024; GEM Wiki Windsor Pulp Mill power station
notes: 609 Rang 12, Windsor, QC. Integrated pulp and paper. $12M Quebec government modernization grant (2024). Recovery boiler is the primary biogenic CO2 point source. Quebec lacks large-scale CO2 storage — low geological storage viability without transport to offshore or saline basins.

name: Irving Pulp & Paper Saint John Mill
capacity_note: 335 kt/yr NBSK+NHBK kraft pulp; undergoing 'NextGen' $1.1B expansion to 1,800 ADt/d (~657 kt/yr)
operator: Irving Pulp & Paper Ltd (J.D. Irving Ltd)
source: Pulp and Paper Canada: Irving NextGen upgrade; Tissue Online: Irving $1.1B upgrade; Irving Pulp and Paper Wikipedia; Paper Age 2024
notes: Saint John, New Brunswick. NextGen project approved 2024: new recovery boiler, steam turbine, lime kiln — jumps production from 1,000 to 1,800 ADt/d. New 140 MW energy output (from 30 MW). The new boiler will be a larger, modern biogenic CO2 point source with potential for CCS integration. Bay of Fundy proximity but limited NB CO2 storage. High retrofit score for new modern recovery boiler being constructed.

name: Canfor Northwood Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~480 kt/yr NBSK (post-2024 curtailment of one line; formerly 510 kt/yr two-line)
source: Canfor press release May 2024 (indefinite curtailment of one line); PulpPaperCanada; Canfor AIF
notes: Prince George, BC. One of two Canfor Prince George facilities (the other is Intercontinental, already in existing DB). One production line curtailed indefinitely May 2024 due to fibre shortage. Reduced-capacity facility still large. Prince George cluster (Northwood + Intercontinental + potential Al-Pac collaboration via pipeline) could support shared CO2 transport.

name: Paper Excellence Crofton Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~355 kt/yr NBSK (pulp continues; paper production indefinitely curtailed Jan 2024)
operator: Paper Excellence Canada (Domtar subsidiary; Crofton closure announced Dec 2025)
source: Crofton Mill Wikipedia; PaperAge Jan 2024; Domtar Dec 2025 closure announcement
notes: Crofton, BC (Vancouver Island, Cowichan Valley). Paper machines indefinitely curtailed Jan 2024; pulp only. Permanent closure announced December 2025 — FACILITY MAY CLOSE. Low retrofit score due to pending closure. Included for completeness as a large historical biogenic CO2 source. If closure confirmed, delist.

name: Resolute Thunder Bay Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~535 kt/yr combined pulp, newsprint, and specialty papers (Thunder Bay, Ontario)
operator: Thunder Bay Pulp and Paper (Atlas Holdings; acquired from Resolute Forest Products Aug 2023)
source: Pulp and Paper Canada: Thunder Bay Pulp and Paper acquires Resolute mill; EUWID Resolute Thunder Bay capacity
notes: Thunder Bay, Northwest Ontario on Lake Superior. Acquired from Resolute by Atlas Holdings affiliate in August 2023 under new operator. Produces market pulp, newsprint, and specialty papers. No CCS plans. Ontario lacks established CO2 storage infrastructure; northwest Ontario is remote from major storage basins.

name: Domtar Ashdown Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: 700 kt/yr total pulp (442 kt fluff + 258 kt SBSK); paper capacity partially idled 2024
source: Domtar Ashdown fact sheet 2025; PulpPaperNews Feb 2024 curtailment; Arkansas EDC case study
notes: 285 Hwy 71, Ashdown, AR 71822 (Little River County). One of North America's largest fluff pulp mills (442 kt fluff + specialty grades). One paper machine idled 2024, but pulp operations continue at scale. Gulf Coast CO2 storage access via pipeline to TX/LA saline formations. High retrofit score: large single-site biogenic CO2 source, proximity to Gulf storage infrastructure.

name: Domtar Plymouth Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~444 kt/yr SBSK fluff pulp; 100% fluff pulp facility (converted 2010)
source: Domtar Plymouth Mill website; Domtar 8-K fluff pulp conversion announcement; WhatTheyThink
notes: Plymouth, Washington County, NC on the Roanoke River. 100% fluff pulp. Nearly 100% renewable energy self-sufficient. No CCS plans. Southeastern US saline aquifer storage available (Deep River Triassic Basin, Atlantic Coastal Plain). Recovery boiler is the primary biogenic CO2 point source.

name: International Paper Pensacola (Cantonment) Mill
capacity_note: ~600 kt/yr SBSK/fluff (reduced from ~1.1 Mt/yr after permanent shutdown of #4 machine Oct 2023)
source: IP 8-K Oct 2023 strategic actions; WKRG.com #4 machine closure; IP Pensacola Mill paper-world.com
notes: 375 Muscogee Road, Cantonment, FL 32533 (Escambia County). #4 machine permanently shut 2023 (−300 kt fluff, −200 kt SBSK). Remaining mill still large-scale kraft pulp. Gulf Coast proximity for CO2 storage. IP is the largest US pulp producer; no company-wide BECCS strategy announced.

name: International Paper Riegelwood Mill
capacity_note: ~500 kt/yr fluff pulp (after #20 machine permanent shutdown end 2023; 2026 expansion planned)
source: IP 8-K Oct 2023 strategic actions; EUWID IP Riegelwood fluff expansion; Resourcewise Riegelwood closure analysis; Pulp and Paper Technology $135M expansion
notes: Riegelwood, Columbus County, NC. Primarily fluff pulp. #20 machine permanently closed end-2023 (−300 kt fluff capacity); 2026 fluff expansion planned. Net capacity decline then recovery. Southeastern US saline storage available. No CCS plans.

name: International Paper Vicksburg Containerboard Mill
capacity_note: ~750 kt/yr containerboard; Mississippi River location
source: IP Vicksburg Containerboard Mill website; GridInfo.com IP Vicksburg Mill black liquor power; calc: ~0.92 t CO2/adt × 750 kt
notes: Vicksburg, Warren County, MS on Mississippi River. Integrated kraft pulping + containerboard. Recovery boiler had explosion in 2008 but facility continues operating. Mississippi River corridor proximity to Gulf Coast CO2 storage infrastructure. High retrofit score for geology and scale.

name: International Paper Bogalusa Containerboard Mill
capacity_note: ~600 kt/yr containerboard (kraft linerboard + medium)
source: IP Bogalusa Containerboard Mill website; Louisiana Economic Development $52M modernization; calc: ~0.92 t CO2/adt
notes: Bogalusa, Washington Parish, LA. Louisiana governor announced $52M modernization. Gulf Coast location — excellent proximity to saline aquifer CO2 storage (Mississippi Embayment, Gulf Coast formations). High retrofit score for geography and ongoing capital investment.

name: Packaging Corp of America Counce Containerboard Mill
capacity_note: ~1.04 Mt/yr kraft linerboard; largest single containerboard mill in US
source: PCA SEC 10-K 2011 capacity data; PCA Counce Mill website; PCA history; calc: ~0.92 t CO2/adt × 1,040 kt
notes: 6715 Highway 57, Counce, TN 38326 (Hardin County). One of the largest US kraft mills by throughput. Integrated kraft pulping with large recovery boiler. Tennessee River / Mississippi River corridor for CO2 transport to Gulf storage. Prime BECCS retrofit candidate given scale and Southern US location.

name: Packaging Corp of America Valdosta Containerboard Mill
capacity_note: ~556 kt/yr kraft linerboard; Valdosta, Georgia
source: PCA SEC 10-K 2011 capacity data; PCA mill listing; calc: ~0.92 t CO2/adt × 556 kt
notes: Valdosta, Lowndes County, GA. Kraft linerboard mill. Southeastern US saline aquifer storage available. No CCS plans. PCA has no stated BECCS strategy.

name: Smurfit WestRock Covington Paperboard Mill
capacity_note: ~950 kt/yr solid bleached sulfate (SBS) paperboard; integrated kraft pulping
source: Smurfit WestRock Covington facility profile 2025; Environmental Integrity Project 'Paper Trail of Pollution' report May 2025; Virginia Mercury June 2025; EPA GHGRP
notes: Covington, Alleghany County, VA. Nation's top GHG emitter among US paper mills in 2023 (970 kt reported + ~1.5 Mt biogenic CO2 excluded from EPA reporting under biogenic exemption = ~2.5 Mt total). Boiler built 1940 — older infrastructure. Total biogenic CO2 est. ~1.5 Mt/yr (from biogenic exemption figures in EIP report). High absolute emissions but aging boiler reduces technical retrofit attractiveness. Appalachian Mountains location complicates CO2 transport.

name: Georgia-Pacific Palatka Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~300 kt/yr kraft paper + tissue; $83M expansion 2025 for tissue capacity
source: GP Palatka Mill profile; Georgia-Pacific Palatka 75th anniversary 2022; Jax Daily Record $83M expansion Apr 2025; Energy Star GP Palatka plant profile
notes: Palatka, Putnam County, FL on St. Johns River. Produces Angel Soft, Brawny, kraft paper, linerboard. $83M expansion 2025 for tissue capacity. Florida location near saline formations. Recovery boiler is biogenic CO2 source. Larger IP and GP operations further south/west in FL/TX dwarf this.

name: Georgia-Pacific Crossett Pulp & Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~300 kt/yr tissue paper + communication grades; $90M expansion 2025-2026 for bath tissue
source: Area Development GP Crossett $90M expansion Dec 2024; CLUI Crossett Paper Mill; GP 10-K historical
notes: Crossett, Ashley County, AR. Ongoing capital investment ($90M bath tissue converting capacity). Gulf Coast geography for CO2 storage. Recovery boiler present (kraft pulping). Smaller than the largest US mills, but active investment site.

name: Sappi Cloquet Mill
capacity_note: ~350 kt/yr coated graphic paper + ~350 kt/yr dissolving wood pulp (Verve brand)
source: Sappi Cloquet Mill website; Sappi $25M investment announcement; Pine Knot News 125th anniversary 2023
notes: Cloquet, Carlton County, MN on the St. Louis River (west of Duluth). Integrated kraft pulp mill producing coated paper and dissolving pulp. $25M investment in pulp capacity. No CCS plans. Minnesota lacks established CO2 storage infrastructure. Biogenic CO2 from recovery boiler and bark/wood waste boilers.

name: Sappi Somerset Mill
capacity_note: ~520 kt/yr SBS board (PM2 converted from coated paper 2025); integrated kraft pulp
source: Sappi Somerset Mill website; PaperAge PM2 rebuild ramp-up 2025; Sappi Project Elevate announcement
notes: Skowhegan, Somerset County, ME. 'Project Elevate': PM2 rebuilt and converted to SBS board production (2025). Kraft pulp mill in situ. Maine is remote from established CO2 storage. Limited CCS infrastructure. No CCS plans. ME/New England biomass + pulp sector has future BECCS potential but no near-term pathway.

name: Pixelle Specialty Solutions Spring Grove Mill
capacity_note: ~240 kt/yr kraft pulp (HW+SW fiberlines, 90% self-supplied); specialty paper
source: Pixelle Spring Grove company profile; PA Chamber Pixelle profile; Gridinfo.com Pixelle black liquor power
notes: Spring Grove, York County, PA. Specialty papers (printing, décor, filtration, packaging). Integrated kraft pulp plant (240 kt/yr). No CCS plans. Mid-Atlantic — some Appalachian Basin storage potential but not well-characterized. Chillicothe OH mill closed Apr 2025.

name: Clearwater Paper Lewiston Pulp & Paperboard Mill
capacity_note: ~460 kt/yr SBS paperboard (continuous digester upgrade; formerly Potlatch/Clearwater Paper); 3 SBS mills total for Clearwater
source: Clearwater Paper Wikipedia; Intermountain Histories Lewiston paper mill; GEM Wiki Lewiston Pulp Mill power station; Clearwater Paper 8-K 2019
notes: Lewiston, Nez Perce County, ID on Snake/Clearwater River confluence. Originally Potlatch Forests (1950). Continuous digester upgrade added 45-55 kt/yr pulp capacity. SBS paperboard products. Pacific Northwest — limited CO2 storage but Snake River Plain deep basalt formations are a potential (same geology as CarbonSafe Snake River Plain). No CCS plans.

name: Reworld (Covanta) Essex Newark WTE
capacity_note: 985,500 t/yr MSW; 65 MWe; Newark, NJ (Essex County)
operator: Reworld (formerly Covanta); owned by Port Authority of NY/NJ
source: Essex County Resource Recovery Facility Wikipedia; Reworld Essex FAQs page; Patch.com emissions data
notes: Adjacent to NJ Turnpike between Raymond Blvd and Passaic River, Newark NJ. 985,500 t/yr; 65 MWe. Opened 1990. Biogenic fraction ~55% (US MSW). Est. biogenic CO2 = 985,500 t/yr × 0.55 biogenic × ~0.5 t CO2/t MSW. Among largest US Northeast WtE plants. No CCS plans.

name: Reworld (Covanta) Fairfax I-95 Energy Facility
capacity_note: 3,000 t/day MSW (1.1 Mt/yr); 80 MWe; Lorton, Virginia
operator: Reworld (formerly Covanta Fairfax Inc.); Fairfax County contract
source: Fairfax County PWES facility description; Covanta Fairfax website; New River Resource Authority regional WTE facilities list
notes: I-95 Energy/Resource Recovery Facility, Lorton, Fairfax County VA. 3,000 t/day; 80 MWe. Serves ~900,000 customers in DC suburbs. No CCS plans. Mid-Atlantic US — limited but growing CO2 storage interest (Potomac Aquifer, offshore Atlantic). Biogenic fraction ~55% US MSW.

name: Reworld (Covanta) SEMASS
capacity_note: >1 Mt/yr MSW (3,000 t/day); Rochester, Massachusetts; shred-and-burn technology
operator: Reworld (formerly Covanta SEMASS); operates for regional municipalities
source: SEMASS Wikipedia; Reworld SEMASS website; Cape Cod Commission Phase One Report
notes: Rochester, Plymouth County, MA. Southeastern Massachusetts Resource Recovery Facility. >1 Mt/yr; 3,000 t/day; generates 25% of MA renewable electricity (~75,000 homes). Shred-and-burn RDF technology. New England WtE sector — no CCS. Massachusetts offshore Atlantic storage potential being explored. Biogenic fraction ~55%.

name: Reworld (Covanta) Hempstead WTE
capacity_note: ~1.01 Mt/yr MSW; 72 MWe; Westbury, New York (Long Island)
operator: Reworld (formerly Covanta Hempstead); Nassau County contract
source: Reworld Hempstead Wikipedia; Covanta Hempstead 30th anniversary press release 2019; Reworld Hempstead website
notes: Westbury, Nassau County, NY (Long Island). ~1.01 Mt/yr; 72 MWe. Long Island's largest WtE. Opened 1989, rebuilt as new facility same site. No CCS. Potential New York Bight offshore CO2 storage being explored for NYC area industrial CCS cluster. Biogenic ~55%.

name: Wheelabrator (WIN Waste) Baltimore WTE
capacity_note: 716,000 t/yr MSW (2,250 t/day); 64.5 MWe; Westport neighborhood, Baltimore MD
operator: WIN Waste Innovations (formerly Wheelabrator Technologies; Macquarie Infrastructure Partners)
source: Wheelabrator Baltimore Wikipedia; WIN Waste Baltimore page; Waste Dive $45M upgrades 2023
notes: Westport, Baltimore, MD. 2,250 t/day; 64.5 MWe. $45M facility upgrades completed 2023. Steam also sold to Veolia district heating. No CCS plans. Mid-Atlantic area — some CO2 storage geology in Appalachian Basin and offshore Atlantic. Biogenic fraction ~55%.

name: Palm Beach Renewable Energy Facility 2 (REF 2)
capacity_note: ~1 Mt/yr MSW (3,000 t/day); 95–100 MWe; West Palm Beach, Florida
operator: Solid Waste Authority (SWA) of Palm Beach County
source: Power Magazine TOP PLANT REF 2 2015; SWA Palm Beach website; NBC Miami WTE facility explainer
notes: 45th Street, West Palm Beach, FL. Commercial operation July 2015. 95 MWe; 3,000 t/day; ~1 Mt/yr. Paired with older REF 1 (62 MW, 850 kt/yr). Florida has saline aquifer CO2 storage potential (Floridan Aquifer System). No CCS plans for REF 2. Florida's high WtE concentration (18 plants) makes it a natural CCS cluster candidate.

name: Palm Beach Renewable Energy Facility 1 (REF 1)
capacity_note: ~850 kt/yr MSW (exceeds 624 kt/yr design); 62 MWe; West Palm Beach, Florida
operator: Solid Waste Authority (SWA) of Palm Beach County / B&W (B&W subsidiary operates)
source: SWA Palm Beach REF 1 page; Babcock & Wilcox Palm Beach REF 1 success story; renewablesinfo.org REF 1
notes: North County area, West Palm Beach FL. RDF (refuse-derived fuel) technology. Opened 1989. Exceeds design capacity (850 kt/yr vs 624 kt/yr design). Biogenic fraction ~55%.

name: Hennepin Energy Recovery Center (HERC)
capacity_note: ~443 kt/yr MSW (1,212 t/day); 39.6 MWe; Minneapolis, Minnesota
source: Hennepin County HERC factsheet; Hennepin County HERC website; Waste Today HERC future discussions
notes: Minneapolis, Hennepin County, MN. 1,212 t/day; 39.6 MWe; ~200,000 MWh/yr. Powers 25,000 homes. County reviewing long-term future of facility. No CCS. Upper Midwest lacks established CO2 storage — ADM Decatur (IL) is nearest major basin. Biogenic fraction ~55%.

name: Spokane Waste-to-Energy Facility
capacity_note: ~292 kt/yr MSW (800 t/day); 22 MWe; Spokane, Washington
operator: City of Spokane Solid Waste Management
source: Spokane WTE fact sheet 2026; Waste Today Spokane carbon capture exploration; Spokesman-Review Jan 2025
notes: Near Spokane International Airport, Spokane, WA. Operational since late 1991. 800 t/day; 22 MWe. ACTIVE CCS EXPLORATION: City seeking $650,000 from WA Climate Commitment Act for CarbonQuest feasibility study. State classifies 60% biogenic / 40% fossil for compliance purposes. Eastern WA basalt formations (Wallula Basalt pilot project nearby) provide promising CO2 mineralization storage. High retrofit interest relative to small size.

name: Durham York Energy Centre (DYEC)
capacity_note: 140 kt/yr MSW (expanding to 160 kt/yr); 17.5 MWe; Clarington, Ontario
operator: Reworld (Covanta operations); owned jointly by Durham and York Regions
source: Durham York Energy Centre website; DYEC capacity increase page; WtERT Canada DYEC profile
notes: Clarington, Durham Region, ON. Canada's largest municipal WtE facility by modern design. Currently 140 kt/yr; EA approval for 160 kt/yr underway. Small absolute biogenic CO2 volume — low retrofit priority despite modern facility. No CCS plans. Ontario lacks geological CO2 storage.

name: Emerald Energy from Waste (EFW) Brampton
capacity_note: 182 kt/yr current; approved expansion to ~900 kt/yr (100 MWe); Brampton, Ontario
source: Emerald EFW website; HAZMAT Management expansion review Jul 2025; National Observer May 2026; Ontario MECP approval Apr 2025
notes: 7656 Bramalea Rd, Brampton, ON. Current 182 kt/yr; MECP approved major expansion to ~900 kt/yr in April 2025. If expansion proceeds, becomes Canada's largest WtE facility. Expansion adds electricity + steam + eventual hydrogen. Biogenic fraction ~55% CA MSW. CO2 value shown is for expanded facility. Ontario CO2 storage constraints remain. High range in est. reflects post-expansion operation.

name: Gainesville Renewable Energy Center (GREC)
capacity_note: 102.5 MWe biomass; ~1 Mt/yr wood waste fuel; Gainesville, Florida
operator: Gainesville Regional Utilities (GRU); operated under long-term PPA
source: Power Technology GREC project profile; Biomass Magazine grand opening; Valmet GREC reference; GRU Biomass Generation page
notes: Gainesville, Alachua County, FL. 102.5 MWe; operational Dec 2013. ~1 Mt/yr biomass fuel (75-mile radius). 30-year PPA with GRU. Florida saline aquifer storage potential. No CCS. Among the largest dedicated biomass power plants in the US South. calc: 102.5 MW × 8,500 hr/yr × 0.74 t CO2/MWhe.

name: Nacogdoches Biomass Power Plant (Austin Energy)
capacity_note: 115 MWe; wood-fired; Sacul, Texas (~230 mi SE of Austin)
operator: Austin Energy (City of Austin utility; acquired from Southern Power 2019 for $460M)
source: Power Technology Nacogdoches; PR Newswire Southern Company largest US biomass plant; Austin Energy acquisition $460M 2019; GEM Wiki
notes: Sacul, Nacogdoches County, TX. 115 MWe; commercial operations June 2012. Formerly Southern Company's 'nation's largest biomass power plant.' Acquired by Austin Energy for $460M in 2019. Long-term PPA. East Texas location — Gulf of Mexico CO2 storage access. No CCS plans. calc: 115 MW × 8,200 hr/yr × 0.76 t CO2/MWhe.

name: Piedmont Green Power Biomass Plant
capacity_note: 55 MWe; ~600 kt/yr wood waste; Barnesville, Georgia
operator: Pacolet Milliken Enterprises LLC (acquired from Atlantic Power Dec 2023)
source: Pacolet Milliken PGP Biomass page; Bioenergy Insight acquisition Jan 2024; GEM Wiki Piedmont Green Power; Power Technology profile
notes: Barnesville, Lamar County, GA (~70 mi SE of Atlanta). 55 MWe; commercial ops 2013. 600 kt/yr wood waste from 30-mile radius. Long-term PPA with Georgia Power. Acquired by Pacolet Milliken Dec 2023. Southeastern US saline storage potential. No CCS plans. calc: 55 MW × 8,500 hr/yr × 0.73 t CO2/MWhe.

name: Atikokan Generating Station (Biomass)
capacity_note: 205 MWe biomass; 90,000 t/yr wood pellets; converted from coal 2014; North America's largest 100% biomass plant
source: OPG Atikokan biomass page; Atikokan GS Wikipedia; EDI Weekly largest NA biomass plant; Canadian Biomass Magazine conversion story
notes: Atikokan, Thunder Bay District, ON. Converted from coal to 100% biomass 2014 ($170M). 15 biomass burners. 90,000 t/yr wood pellets (largest industrial wood pellet consumer in Canada). Capacity factor lower than coal (~40–50%) due to intermittent operation/dispatch. calc based on 205 MW × ~6,200 hr/yr × ~1.0 t CO2/MWhe. Ontario lacks CO2 storage — major constraint for BECCS. Approved for additional 5 years of operation. Remote NW Ontario location.

name: Kruger Biomass Cogeneration — Brompton & Wayagamack
capacity_note: Combined ~150 MWe biomass CHP across two Kruger pulp/paper facilities; Trois-Rivières and Brompton, Quebec
source: Kruger Incorporated operations website; Pulp and Paper Canada mill directory; Kruger Wayagamack Wikipedia
notes: Wayagamack (Trois-Rivières) and Brompton (Windsor, QC) paper mills with biomass-fired cogeneration. Pulp/paper operations produce biogenic CO2 from recovery boilers AND separate biomass power boilers. Quebec biomass CHP cluster but no CO2 storage infrastructure. Low retrofit score due to storage constraints. Coordinates represent centroid between two sites.

name: Resolute Forest Products Saint-Félicien Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~290 kt/yr NBSK kraft pulp; Lac-Saint-Jean, Quebec
source: Resolute Forest Products mill listing; Resolute 2023 annual report; calc: ~0.92 t CO2/adt × 290 kt
notes: Saint-Félicien, Lac-Saint-Jean, QC. One of Resolute's remaining Quebec kraft mills (many others closed 2012–2023). Quebec lacks geological CO2 storage. Low retrofit score. Resolute sold Thunder Bay mill (2023) — continuing to rationalize capacity.

name: International Paper Georgetown Specialty Paper Mill
capacity_note: ~300 kt/yr specialty papers + containerboard; Georgetown, South Carolina
source: IP Georgetown Paper Mill website; CLUI Georgetown Paper Mill; GridInfo IP Georgetown Mill black liquor power
notes: Georgetown, Georgetown County, SC on Winyah Bay. Specialty papers and containerboard. Integrated kraft pulping with recovery boiler. Southeastern US saline storage accessible. No CCS plans.

name: Domtar Espanola Pulp Mill
capacity_note: ~215 kt/yr NBSK kraft pulp; Espanola, Ontario
source: Domtar mill locations all-locations page; Pulp and Paper Canada Espanola; Canadian NBSK mill database
notes: Espanola, Sudbury District, ON on Spanish River. NBSK kraft pulp. Ontario lacks geological CO2 storage. Low retrofit score. Part of Domtar's Canadian mill network (alongside Ashdown, Plymouth, Windsor).

name: Millar Western Whitecourt BCTMP Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 350 kt/yr BCTMP (bleached chemi-thermomechanical pulp); 20 grades HW+SW; co-located green energy facility
source: Millar Western pulp mill page (millarwestern.com); Alberta CSA Registries GHGR facility listing (FacilityId 392); Pulp and Paper Canada BCTMP article
notes: Whitecourt, Alberta (Woodlands County). BCTMP (chemi-thermomechanical) process — different from kraft; no black liquor recovery boiler. Biogenic CO2 primarily from wood-fired steam boilers (green energy facility) and wood drying. Lower CO2 intensity per tonne of pulp than kraft mills (~0.63 t CO2/adt est. vs. ~0.92 for kraft). Operational since 1988; expanded to 350 kt/yr. Alberta deep saline storage potential (Nisku, Wabamun formations). No CCS plans. Registered under Alberta GHGR.

name: Kruger Pulp & Paper Kamloops (formerly Domtar, now Kruger)
capacity_note: ~50 MWe biomass cogeneration at Kamloops kraft mill
source: GEM Wiki Powell River Pulp Mill power station; Kruger Kamloops acquisition; Domtar Kamloops biomass cogen
notes: Biomass cogeneration boiler co-located with Kamloops kraft pulp mill (separate entry covers the pulp mill's recovery boiler CO2). BC lacks CO2 storage. Low retrofit score. Combined biogenic CO2 from cogen boiler estimated here; recovery boiler CO2 in the Mercer/Domtar Kamloops entry.

name: Pratt Industries Shreveport Containerboard Mill
capacity_note: ~400 kt/yr containerboard (recycled fiber TMP/kraft); Shreveport, Louisiana
source: Pratt Industries Shreveport plant listing; Louisiana manufacturing directory; calc: TMP/kraft mixed process
notes: Shreveport, Caddo Parish, LA. Primarily recycled-fiber containerboard — lower biogenic CO2 than virgin kraft mills (no black liquor recovery boiler at full scale). Some biogenic CO2 from biomass-fired boilers. Gulf Coast proximity is favorable for CO2 storage in principle but limited biogenic CO2 makes this a lower-priority retrofit candidate than virgin kraft mills. Low retrofit score.

name: Tolko Industries Heffley Creek Pulp Mill (formerly Weyerhaeuser)
capacity_note: ~100 kt/yr NBSK pulp; Heffley Creek, BC (Kamloops area)
source: Tolko Industries Heffley Creek mill page; PulpPaperCanada mill map 2021; BC mill database
notes: Heffley Creek, Thompson-Nicola RD, BC. Small kraft pulp mill. BC lacks CO2 storage. Low retrofit score. Smaller of BC interior mills.

name: Enviva Ahoskie Wood Pellet Plant
capacity_note: ~315 kt/yr industrial wood pellets; Ahoskie, North Carolina
source: Enviva Ahoskie plant page; Enviva annual report 2022; Bioenergy International
notes: Ahoskie, Hertford County, NC. Wood pellet manufacturing (not combustion). CO2 from onsite drying kilns and boilers (biogenic), not from combustion of the pellets. Low retrofit score — CO2 source is small and diffuse. Enviva filed Chapter 11 2024, restructuring. Listed for completeness as large woody biomass processing point source; the real biogenic CO2 source is wherever the pellets are burned (e.g., Drax UK).

name: Georgia Biomass Wood Pellet Plant (Waycross)
capacity_note: ~750 kt/yr industrial wood pellets; Waycross, Georgia (world's largest pellet plant at opening)
operator: Drax Group plc (acquired from RWE Group 2019)
source: Drax annual report 2023 (Georgia Biomass supply chain); Biomass Magazine Georgia Biomass; GEM Wiki
notes: Waycross, Ware County, GA. ~750 kt/yr pellets. Owned by Drax (supplies ~20% of Drax UK pellets). CO2 from onsite drying operations. Not a combustion CO2 source — biogenic CO2 is captured when Drax burns pellets in the UK. Low retrofit score for this US facility (the CCS is at Drax UK). Included to note the US pellet supply chain origin of Drax BECCS.

name: Reworld (Covanta) Indianapolis Resource Recovery
capacity_note: ~350 kt/yr MSW (2,175 t/day peak); ~6.5 MWe; Indianapolis, Indiana
operator: Reworld (formerly Covanta); Marion County Solid Waste Management District
source: Database.earth Covanta Indianapolis; EIA Kids field trip Covanta; IN.gov IURC Covanta comments
notes: Indianapolis, Marion County, IN. Operational Dec 1988. 2,175 t/day peak; ~6.5 MWe electric (modest); steam sold. One of the smaller Reworld plants. Illinois Basin CO2 storage (Mt. Simon Sandstone) in proximity — same formation as ADM Decatur. Low retrofit score due to small absolute CO2 volume and aging facility.

name: Drax Morehouse BioEnergy (Louisiana Biomass)
capacity_note: ~450 kt/yr wood pellets + biomass-fired generation (combined pellet manufacturing + power); Bastrop, Louisiana
operator: Drax Group plc (via Drax Biomass Inc.)
source: Drax Group annual report 2023; Drax Biomass Louisiana operations; GEM Wiki Drax Morehouse
notes: Bastrop, Morehouse Parish, LA. One of Drax's largest US pellet production facilities. Pellet drying and manufacturing releases biogenic CO2 (from wood drying steam boilers). Like Georgia Biomass (Waycross GA), the major biogenic CO2 release is at Drax UK where pellets are burned. Louisiana Gulf Coast location = excellent CO2 storage geography but the on-site CO2 source from drying is modest. Low retrofit score — the key BECCS opportunity for Drax biomass is at the UK combustion end, not these US manufacturing plants.
